caption: Each input pulse makes exactly one lit TNT and throws it away: it lands 14 to 18 blocks from the machine and explodes there, and a TNT blast cannot break anything more than about 7 blocks away, so the machine is safe standing right on the ground. Detail: the switchable 12-block engine with a slime launcher (each TNT flung at 1 block per tick) and an active-low input (at rest a redstone block in the input spot holds the piston out; the pulse takes it away for one push); one obsidian foot under the piston keeps the moving slimes off the grass (a slime frame resting on grass drags it). Measured on redsim at every kick angle: on grass the explosions are 14.2 to 18.5 blocks away, on obsidian 14.2; 0 machine blocks destroyed

The TNT duplicator: 86 lit TNT a minute, standing right on the ground, and no explosion ever touches it. Each TNT is thrown away at 1 block per tick and explodes on the ground 9 to 30 blocks off, where it breaks blocks, beyond the 7 blocks a blast reaches. It is two catalog parts: the 16-block duplicator engine, which makes one TNT each time its piston loses power for a moment, and a 6-block clock from the clock catalog (period 14 ticks) whose redstone block holds that piston and steps away for 4 ticks of every 14. Detail: robust over every kick angle on both grounds on redsim (and 64 runs with every TNT its own kick), 16 builds in the game; a period-10 clock gives 120 a minute but lands blasts 5.3 blocks away and fails about 1 game build in 30.
